criminal_detail: Former correctional deputy Christian Heidecker was charged in September 2023 with 18 felony counts; he pleaded guilty in February 2024 to 13 felony charges (four counts of extortion, four counts of dissuading a witness, four counts of soliciting a bribe as a peace officer, and one count of engaging in a sex act as a detention officer) and was sentenced in March 2024 to five years in state prison. He had resigned from the department on September 15, 2023.

description: Seven women who had been incarcerated or on home confinement in Riverside County filed seven separate federal lawsuits in U.S. District Court in Riverside in late March 2024 over sexual abuse and extortion by former Riverside County Sheriff's Department correctional deputy Christian Heidecker. Heidecker pleaded guilty in February 2024 to 13 felonies, including extortion, dissuading witnesses, soliciting bribes, and engaging in a sex act as a detention officer, and was sentenced to five years in state prison. The lawsuits allege that county officials, including Correctional Sergeant Jessica Yelenich and a county attorney, compiled a list of Heidecker's victims and offered them money — in one case a $5,000 check tied to a settlement release — in a scheme to keep them from suing or coming forward. According to the complaints, victims were lured to sheriff's substations under false pretenses and pressured to sign settlement agreements without legal representation. The county disputed that characterization, saying pre-litigation settlements are routine and contain no non-disclosure language. A separate suit on behalf of another victim of the alleged 'hush money' scheme was announced by the firm Taylor & Ring in September 2023.
